About Me

My name is Rishab Narayanan. I am 16 years old going into my junior year at Saratoga High School at the time of making this website. My professional interests lie with electrical engineering and chip design. In my personal life, I have been playing the trumpet since 5th grade, I participate in marching and concert band, and have been playing basketball since 4th grade, all for my school. I also enjoy driving, hanging out with my friends, and playing videogames on my PC that I built in the summer of 2021. On a side note, that PC is very special to me not only because I built it, but because of how I arrived to the building process. During that time, there was the pandemic and the prices of everything had sky-rocketed, especially GPUs, as a result of a chip shortage. I made a deal with my dad that school year, saying that if I got all A's, we could buy the parts to build the computer within a budget. Unfornately, the RTX 3070, the one of the newest and hottest GPUs that just of the time that I wanted to complement my Ryzen 5 5600 CPU did not fall within that budget because of the chip shortage, so I decided to email Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia to request that specific card at regular price, thinking it wouldn't hurt. Suprisingly, Tim Bender, the VP of Consumer and Business Development replied, asking me to forward my parents' contact info to help me obtain the card at regular price. I eventually received it and I was super proud for pursuing my dream and not giving up on it. This website is a result of my desire to put every one of my projects in one place for people to see them and to see how far I have come!

My Projects

Here, you can view all of the projects I have completed, top to bottom, starting with the most recent and advanced one. For each one, there will be a picture of the project, along with a short description of it. These projects are pure software, pure hardware, and a mix of both!

Click the image to view my presentation!

In this project, we were given 2 csv files, one with our images, and one with all our vectors, either attentive or 3 different types of distracted driving: checking mirror, drinking coffee, or using radio. We first split our data into 80% training to develop our model and 20% percent testing to see how it performs. The first model we made was a neural networl, which was only 50% percent accurate. Next, we made a CNN, which was better and gave us 73% accuracy. Finally, we used an expert-trained model already loaded with lots and lots of training data, called transfer learning, and got 84% accuracy. In the end, we deplyed our model to an app using ngrok. Our app takes in an image and outputs what the driver is doing, whether attentive or distracted, and which type of distraced if applicable.
